_comment: What a HUMAN says each photograph is. A declared view beats a guessed one.
_why: make_textures.py picks the plan view by matching a photo's silhouette aspect to the
part's published w:d. That is an honest heuristic and it works -- CK-117TR scores 1%
error, and it correctly REFUSES CK-116TL and CK-117TL at 62-66% because their
galleries genuinely have no plan view. But it is still a guess, it cannot tell a
top-down shot from an underside shot, and it cannot see an image nobody gave it.
It cost us: I read the plan view as the UNDERSIDE (brackets and hooks are visible in
it, and where else would brackets be?), moved the photo beneath the board, and built
a grain-crop for the top face to cover for it. Snow Peak's own studio shot (JP a099)
says otherwise: the bracket plates sit ON the bamboo, because the NEXT board's wire
hooks have to drop into them from above, and the leg screws up into the same plate
from below. The user said it was the top view. The user was right.
So: look at the images in the part bench, say what each one is, and write it here.
A sentence from someone who owns the part beats a heuristic every time.

_schema.note: 'plan_top' is the one make_textures.py wants: flat, orthographic, on white.

CK-218._said: top view; the hooks are on the RIGHT edge, the bracket plates on the left. a009 is the hook close-up: a stainless wire hook let into a slot in the board's edge, arching out and bending straight DOWN -- it hangs over the host's edge from above.
